title: EdDSA (Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm)
summary: EdDSA is a digital signature scheme using twisted Edwards curves. Ed25519 (RFC 8032) uses Curve25519. Signing: hash the message with the private key, derive a nonce, compute R = r*G, S = r + H(R||A||M)*a mod l. Signature = (R, S) (64 bytes). Verification: check S*G == R + H(R||A||M)*A. Deterministic (no random nonce needed).

structure.meaning: Random 32 bytes. Hashed to derive scalar a and nonce prefix.
A = a*G (point on Curve25519). Compressed (x-coordinate only).
R (32 bytes, compressed point) + S (32 bytes, scalar). R = r*G, S = (r + H(R||A||M)*a) mod l.
H = SHA-512. Used for both nonce derivation and signature computation.
r = SHA-512(private_key_prefix || message) mod l. Deterministic (no RNG needed for signing).
Check S*G == R + H(R||A||M)*A. If equal, signature is valid.

notes: Ed25519 is the most common EdDSA variant (RFC 8032).
EdDSA is deterministic: no random nonce needed for signing (unlike ECDSA).
Ed25519 is faster than ECDSA (no modular inverse needed).
Ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes (vs 70-72 bytes for ECDSA P-256).
EdDSA is used in SSH, TLS 1.3, Signal, and many modern systems.
